questions.prompt: Which animal says "moo"?
questions.explain: Cows say moo.

questions.prompt: What do plants need to grow?
questions.explain: Plants drink water and use sunlight.

questions.prompt: Which of these is hot?
questions.explain: The sun warms the Earth.

questions.prompt: How many legs does a dog have?
questions.explain: Dogs walk on four legs.

questions.prompt: Which of these can fly?
questions.explain: Birds have wings.

questions.prompt: What do we use our eyes for?
questions.explain: Eyes are for seeing.

questions.prompt: Which part of your body do you smell with?
questions.explain: Your nose smells.

questions.prompt: Which animal lives in the water?
questions.explain: Fish breathe underwater.

questions.prompt: Which season is usually the coldest?
questions.explain: Winter is the coldest season.

questions.prompt: What is a baby cat called?
questions.explain: A baby cat is a kitten.

questions.prompt: What does a caterpillar turn into?
questions.explain: Caterpillars become butterflies.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a fruit?
questions.explain: Apples grow on trees and have seeds.

questions.prompt: Which planet do we live on?
questions.explain: We live on planet Earth.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a reptile?
questions.explain: Reptiles have dry, scaly skin.

questions.prompt: What do bees make?
questions.explain: Bees make honey from nectar.

questions.prompt: What does ice become when it melts?
questions.explain: Melting turns solid ice into liquid water.

questions.prompt: Which part of a plant takes in water from the soil?
questions.explain: Roots soak up water.

questions.prompt: How many continents are there?
questions.explain: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America, South America.

questions.prompt: How many planets are in our solar system?
questions.explain: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

questions.prompt: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.explain: The Sun is a star, and it is our closest one.

questions.prompt: Water vapour is water in which state?
questions.explain: Vapour is a gas.

questions.prompt: What do herbivores eat?
questions.explain: Herbi- means plant: cows and rabbits are herbivores.

questions.prompt: Which continent is Egypt in?
questions.explain: Egypt is in north-east Africa.

questions.prompt: What do we call water falling from clouds?
questions.explain: Rain, snow and hail are precipitation.

questions.prompt: Which gas do plants take in from the air to make food?
questions.explain: Plants take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen.

questions.prompt: What is the hardest natural substance?
questions.explain: Diamond is the hardest known natural material.

questions.prompt: Which organ pumps blood around your body?
questions.explain: The heart is a muscle that pumps blood.

questions.prompt: What force pulls things toward the Earth?
questions.explain: Gravity makes things fall down.

questions.prompt: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explain: Mars looks red because of iron oxide (rust) in its soil.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of France?
questions.explain: Paris is the capital city of France.

questions.prompt: What is the process plants use to make their own food from light?
questions.explain: Photo = light. Plants make sugar from light, water and CO₂.

questions.prompt: At what temperature (°C) does pure water boil at sea level?
questions.explain: Water boils at 100 °C (212 °F).

questions.prompt: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explain: The Pacific covers about a third of the planet.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a renewable energy source?
questions.explain: The Sun keeps shining, so solar power does not run out.

questions.prompt: Animals that eat both plants and meat are called…
questions.explain: Omni means all. Humans and bears are omnivores.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical formula of water?
questions.explain: Two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

questions.prompt: Which part of a cell is called its "powerhouse"?
questions.explain: Mitochondria release energy from food.

questions.prompt: Which planet is famous for its bright rings?
questions.explain: Saturn has the biggest, brightest ring system.

questions.prompt: About how fast does light travel?
questions.explain: Light is the fastest thing in the universe.

questions.prompt: Which blood cells help fight infection?
questions.explain: White blood cells are the body's defenders.

questions.prompt: Rock that forms when lava cools is called…
questions.explain: Igneous comes from the Latin for fire.

questions.prompt: How many bones does an adult human have?
questions.explain: Babies are born with about 300 that fuse together.

questions.prompt: Which element has the chemical symbol "Fe"?
questions.explain: Fe comes from the Latin word ferrum.

questions.prompt: Newton's third law says that every action has…
questions.explain: Pushing a wall pushes you back just as hard.

questions.prompt: What is the pH of a neutral substance like pure water?
questions.explain: Below 7 is acidic; above 7 is basic.

questions.prompt: Which gas makes up most of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explain: About 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen.

questions.prompt: What shape is the DNA molecule?
questions.explain: Two strands twist around each other.

questions.prompt: Which ancient civilization built the pyramids at Giza?
questions.explain: They were built about 4,500 years ago as tombs.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explain: 1 newton accelerates 1 kg by 1 m/s every second.

questions.prompt: Which particle has a negative charge?
questions.explain: Electrons orbit the nucleus.

questions.prompt: Which formula gives speed?
questions.explain: Speed = distance ÷ time.

questions.prompt: Which part of a plant cell contains chlorophyll?
questions.explain: Chloroplasts capture light and make it green.

questions.prompt: What is the main cause of ocean tides?
questions.explain: The Moon's pull makes the water bulge.

questions.prompt: What is the most abundant element in the universe?
questions.explain: Stars are mostly hydrogen.

questions.prompt: Ohm's law links voltage, current and…
questions.explain: V = I × R.

questions.prompt: Cell division that makes two identical copies of a body cell is called…
questions.explain: Mitosis is how you grow and heal.

questions.prompt: A bond where atoms share electrons is called…
questions.explain: Water molecules are held together by covalent bonds.

questions.prompt: Which type of wave has the shortest wavelength?
questions.explain: Gamma rays carry the most energy.

questions.prompt: What do we call the large slabs that make up Earth's outer shell?
questions.explain: Their movement causes earthquakes and volcanoes.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of energy?
questions.explain: Named after James Prescott Joule.
